interrupt.d: To disturb or halt (an ongoing process or action, or the person performing it) by interfering suddenly, especially by speaking.
interrupt.e: The interrupt caused the packet handler routine to run.

interval.e: the interval between contractions during childbirth

interviewee.d: Someone being interviewed, i.e. the person answering the questions.

introduction.d: The act or process of introducing.
introduction.e: the introduction of a new product into the market

invasion.d: The forcible entry of armed forces into another state’s territory, typically for the purpose of conquest, occupation, or establishing control.

invest.d: To spend money, time, or energy on something, especially for some benefit or purpose; used with in.
invest.e: We'd like to thank all the contributors who have invested countless hours into this event.

invitation.d: The act of inviting; solicitation; the requesting of a person's company.
invitation.e: an invitation to a party, to a dinner, or to visit a friend

involuntarily.d: In an involuntary manner; done without conscious thought.

involve.d: To roll or fold up; to wind round; to entwine.
involve.e: to involve in darkness or obscurity

involved.e: He related an involved story about every ancestor since 1895.

iron.d: A common, inexpensive metal, silvery grey when untarnished, that rusts, is attracted by magnets, and is used in making steel.
iron.e: He held on with an iron grip.

irregular.d: A soldier who is not a member of an official military force and, often, does not follow regular army tactics

isle.d: An island, usually very small. Compare with islet.

isolation.d: The state of being isolated, detached, or separated; the state of being away from other people.
isolation.e: She lived her final year in complete isolation, not wanting to see anybody.

jar.d: An earthenware container, either with two or no handles, for holding oil, water, wine, etc., or used for burial.

jazz.d: A musical art form rooted in West African cultural and musical expression and in the African American blues tradition, with diverse influences over time, commonly characterized by blue notes, syncopation, swing, call and response, polyrhythms and improvisation.
jazz.e: You’ve gone and jazzed it now!

joint.d: The point where two components of a structure join, but are still able to rotate.
joint.e: This rod is free to swing at the joint with the platform.

journalist.d: The keeper of a personal journal, who writes in it regularly.

jug.d: A serving vessel or container, typically circular in cross-section and typically higher than it is wide, with a relatively small mouth or spout, an ear handle and often a stopper or top.

jumper.d: Someone or something that jumps, e.g. a participant in a jumping event in track or skiing.

justice.d: The state or characteristic of being just or fair.

kettle.d: A vessel for boiling a liquid or cooking food, usually metal and equipped with a lid.
kettle.e: There's a hot kettle of soup on the stove.

keyboard.d: A set of keys laid out in a gridlike pattern, used for typing on a typewriter, computer, etc.
keyboard.e: Keyboarding is the part of this job I hate the most.

killing.d: That literally deprives of life; lethal, deadly, fatal.

kindness.e: How can I thank you for your many kindnesses?

kitten.d: A young cat, especially before sexual maturity (reached at about seven months).

knit.e: The first generation knitted to order; the second still knits for its own use; the next leaves knitting to industrial manufacturers.

lab.e: I dropped my mixture while doing my lab, so I had to start over.

laboratory.d: A room, building or institution equipped for scientific research, experimentation or analysis.

ladder.d: A frame, usually portable, of wood, metal, or rope, used for ascent and descent, consisting of two side pieces to which are fastened rungs (cross strips or rounds acting as steps).

lamb.e: The shepherd was up all night, lambing her young ewes.

landlord.d: A person who owns and rents land such as a house, apartment, or condo.

largely.d: In a widespread or large manner.
largely.e: They were largely successful in their efforts.

lasting.d: Persisting for an extended period of time.
lasting.e: After World War I it was hoped that a lasting peace had been achieved. It hadn’t.

latecomer.d: One who has arrived comparatively recently.
latecomer.e: The old families in the neighborhood look down on him as a latecomer, his family only arrived in the 18th century, too nouveau for them.

lately.d: Recently; not long ago; of late; not long since.

laughter.d: The sound of laughing, produced by air so expelled; any similar sound.
laughter.e: Their loud laughter betrayed their presence.

launch.d: The movement of a vessel from land into the water; especially, the sliding on ways from the stocks on which it is built. (Compare: to splash a ship.)

layer.d: A single thickness of some material covering a surface.
layer.e: After the first coat of paint dried, he applied another layer.

leading.d: To cover, fill, or affect with lead
leading.e: Avoid leading questions if you really want the truth.

lean.d: (of an object taller than its width and depth) An inclination away from the vertical.
lean.e: The trees had various leans toward gaps in the canopy.

leap.d: The act of leaping or jumping.
leap.e: to leap a wall or a ditch

lecture.d: A spoken lesson or exposition, usually delivered to a group.
lecture.e: During class today the professor delivered an interesting lecture.

legal.d: The legal department of a company.

length.d: The distance measured along the longest dimension of an object.

lessen.d: To make less; to diminish; to reduce.

librarian.d: The keeper, manager of a library.

lightly.e: As a teacher, I don't take rudeness in class lightly.

lightning.d: A flash of light produced by short-duration, high-voltage discharge of electricity within a cloud, between clouds, or between a cloud and the earth.
lightning.e: Although we did not see the lightning, we did hear the thunder.

limit.d: A restriction; a bound beyond which one may not go.
limit.e: The sequence of reciprocals has zero as its limit.

limited.d: simple past and past participle of limit
limited.e: There are limited places available. Enrol now or you will miss out.

link.d: Some text or a graphic in an electronic document that can be activated to display another document or trigger an action.
link.e: The mayor’s assistant serves as the link to the media.

literature.d: The body of all written works.

liver.d: A large organ in the body that stores and metabolizes nutrients, destroys toxins and produces bile. It is responsible for thousands of biochemical reactions.
liver.e: Steve Jobs is a famous liver transplant recipient.

loaf.d: (also loaf of bread) A block of bread after baking.

locate.d: To place; to set in a particular spot or position.

location.d: A particular point or place in physical space.

logic.d: A method of human thought that involves thinking in a linear, step-by-step manner about how a problem can be solved. Logic is the basis of many principles including the scientific method.

loss.d: The result of no longer possessing an object, a function, or a characteristic due to external causes or misplacement.
loss.e: In other areas, glacier loss creates serious risk of a dry period across the Third Pole, Wang said.

loud.d: A loud sound or part of a sound.
loud.e: Turn that music down; it's too loud.

loyal.d: Having or demonstrating undivided and constant support for someone or something.

luggage.d: The bags and other containers that hold a traveller's belongings.

lung.d: A biological organ of vertebrates that controls breathing and oxygenates the blood.
lung.e: He hasn't the lungs to play long rallies like he use to.

magnificent.d: Grand, elegant or splendid in appearance.

maintenance.d: Actions performed to keep some machine or system functioning or in service.

management.d: Administration; the use of limited resources combined with forecasting, planning, leadership and execution skills to achieve predetermined specific goals.

marine.d: A soldier, normally a member of a marine corps, trained to serve on board or from a ship
marine.e: He was a marine in World War II.

marriage.e: You should enter marriage for love.

massive.d: A homogeneous mass of rock, not layered and without an obvious crystal structure.
massive.e: Big up to the Croydon massive!

measure.d: A prescribed quantity or extent. Moderation, temperance. A limit that cannot be exceeded; a bound. (Now chiefly in set phrases.)

mechanic.d: A manual worker; a labourer or artisan.

mechanical.d: Manually created layout of artwork that is camera ready for photographic reproduction.

medium.d: The material of the surrounding environment, e.g. solid, liquid, gas, vacuum, or a specific substance such as a solvent.

melt.d: Molten material, the product of melting.
melt.e: I melted butter to make a cake.

membership.d: The state of being a member of a group or organization.
membership.e: He has memberships in clubs in three cities.

memorable.d: Worthy to be remembered; very important or remarkable.

memorise.d: Non-Oxford British English standard spelling of memorize.

memorize.d: To fully learn so as to have entirely available to the memory; to learn by heart, commit to memory.

mend.d: To physically repair (something that is broken, defaced, decayed, torn, or otherwise damaged).
mend.e: My trousers have a big rip in them and need a mend.
